catalog_quote: Stress normally falls on the second mora of words with three or more moras, as shown in (3) and (4), which suggests a peninitial pattern. ... a. panóko ‘five’ ... a. simpénoi ‘naked’ ... As can be observed in the data above, there is no evidence to suggest that coda consonants are moraic in the system, because stress does not shift as a function of the presence or absence of codas (e.g., [simpénoi] ‘naked’). ... Observe the bimoraic forms in (5), which have stress on the first vowel: ... a. báɾeŋ ‘bird’ ... This is apparently an avoidance of stress on the final mora in words. ... In terms of stress placement, long vowels are treated as if they were sequences; that is, each vowel portion counts as a stress bearing unit (Hurd & Hurd 1970). tone.quote: These generalisations around stress are largely due to Hurd & Hurd (1970), though independent data were collected and observed spectrographically. Stress acoustically involves a peak in F0 and amplitude. For forms which do not involve long vowels, this also involves an increase in duration. … even if the acoustic cues turn out to be correlates of an accentual system, this does not nullify the results here … Acoustic evidence suggests that in words with five or more moras, there is a stress on the second mora, and no other detectable pitch peaks or durational differences.
tone.summary: No tone analysis: pitch is treated only as a correlate of word stress (F0 peak on the stressed second mora, no other pitch peaks); the author allows the cues might reflect an accentual system.
tone.says: No tone analysis: pitch is treated only as a correlate of word stress (F0 peak on the stressed second mora, no other pitch peaks); the author allows the cues might reflect an accentual system.

sources.quote: 'Identical vowels occur in sequences of up to four and are pronounced as varying degrees of length ... there are no individual syllabic peaks unless one of the vowels is stressed, in which case the stressed vowel has a higher pitch. ... Stress is nonphonemic. With words in isolation it occurs on the first syllable of two-syllable words and on the second syllable of words of three or more syllables.' (Their 'syllable' counts each vowel of a VV sequence separately, i.e. = Brown's mora; codas do not add syllables.) Also sec. 11.1: 'anta does not take stress independent of the preceding stem'.

The length corresponds to the number of identical vowels; there are no individual syllabic peaks unless one of the vowels is stressed, in which case the stressed vowel has a higher pitch. tone.summary: No tone: pitch is mentioned only as the realisation of nonphonemic word stress (higher pitch on the stressed vowel); stress on the 1st syllable of disyllables and the 2nd syllable of longer words (Naasioi Proper).

tone.quote: Der dynamische Akzent wird im nachstehenden mit dem Zeichen ’ kennbar gemacht. Sehr wichtig ist es, jedes Wort richtig zu betonen; denn je nach der Tonstellung erhalt das Wort manchmal eine ganz andere Bedeutung, z. B.: kara Liebe, kdra Mond … In manchen zweisilbigen Wértern stehen beide Silben auf gleicher Ton- stufe, wie dua Sonne, karan Krebs … Wenn ein drei- oder mehrsilbiges Wort den Akzent auf der zweiten (bzw. dritten) Silbe hat, so ist diese Silbe hochtonig und auch alle vorhergehenden Silben sind hochtonig; die ihr nachfolgenden Silben dagegen sind tieftonig.
tone.locator: p. 107, A. Die Nasioi-Sprache, I. Lautlehre, d Akzent
tone.translation: The dynamic accent is marked below with the sign ’. It is very important to stress every word correctly, for depending on the accent position the word sometimes gets a quite different meaning, e.g. kara love vs. kára moon … In some disyllabic words both syllables stand on the same pitch level, as dua sun, karan crab … When a word of three or more syllables has the accent on the second (or third) syllable, that syllable is high-toned and all preceding syllables are also high-toned; the syllables following it are by contrast low-toned.
tone.summary: Describes a contrastive dynamic (stress) accent; pitch follows it: the accented syllable and all before it high, those after it low; some disyllables level and weakly stressed. No tone inventory.
tone.says: Describes a contrastive dynamic (stress) accent; pitch follows it: the accented syllable and all before it high, those after it low; some disyllables level and weakly stressed. No tone inventory.
